title: Finite affine refinement and base-ideal factors for etale local module flatifications
statement:
Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, $U\subset S$ a quasi-compact open, $f:X\to S$ a morphism of schemes, and $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module. Let $I$ be a finite index set and, for every $i\in I$, let $g_i:X_i\to S_i$, $e_i:S_i\to S$ and $j_i:X_i\to X$ satisfy $e_i g_i=fj_i$. Assume $e_i$ is quasi-compact and etale, $j_i$ is etale, and both families $(e_i)$ and $(j_i)$ are jointly surjective, meaning that every point of the target lies in some image. For each $i$ let $\mathcal J_i\subset\mathcal O_{S_i}$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal, equal to the unit ideal on $U_i=e_i^{-1}U$, such that the strict transform of $j_i^*\mathcal F$ under $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J_i}S_i\to S_i$ is flat over $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J_i}S_i$.

There are a finite set $R$, a map $i:R\to I$, and affine open subschemes $W_r\subset S_{i(r)}$ with $S_i=\bigcup_{i(r)=i}W_r$. Put $Y_r=X_{i(r)}\times_{S_{i(r)}}W_r$ and $\mathcal J_r=\mathcal J_{i(r)}|_{W_r}$. The induced maps $W_r\to S$ are quasi-compact and etale and jointly surjective, and $Y_r\to X$ are etale and jointly surjective. Each $W_r$ is qcqs. The restricted blowup is $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J_r}W_r$, is $(W_r\times_SU)$-admissible, and its module strict transform is canonically the restriction of the given flat transform, hence is flat over that blowup.

If additionally $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $U=D(a)$ for an element $a\in A$ whose multiplication map on $A$ is injective, the refinement can be chosen with, for each $r$, a finitely generated ideal $I_r\subset A$ and a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal J'_r\subset\mathcal O_{W_r}$ such that
$$V(I_r)\subset V(a),\qquad I_r\mathcal O_{W_r}=\mathcal J_r\mathcal J'_r.$$
Here $V(I)$ denotes the primes containing $I$ and $D(a)$ its complement for the principal ideal $(a)$. Schemes, qcqs conventions, quasi-coherence, relative module flatness, admissible blowups, module strict transforms, fibre products and module pullbacks are as in [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], [pqf-def-coherent], [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over], [def-nagata-admissible-blowup], [def-trf-module-strict-transform], [def-pc-fibre-product] and [def-pc-module-pullback]. Etale morphisms and affine spectra are as in [def-weil-etale-morphism] and [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Blowups themselves are those of [def-nagata-global-blowup].

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-morphism-preimage-qc-open] to $e_i$ and the quasi-compact open $S\subset S$: every $S_i$ is quasi-compact. Choose a finite affine open cover $S_i=\bigcup_t T_{it}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-finite-affine-open-cover]. In the general case these will be the $W_r$. In the additional affine-base case we refine each $T_{it}$ further in the next two steps. All the preliminary opens $T_{it}$ are quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs].

source.place: Tag 0814, lemma-flatten-module-etale-localize, proof paragraph 2 (finite open refinement); Tag 0813, lemma-push-ideal.

proof.text: Now assume $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $U=D(a)$ with $a$ a nonzerodivisor. Fix $T=T_{it}=\operatorname{Spec}B$. The inclusion $T\hookrightarrow S_i$ and then $e_i$ compose to an etale map by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Set $J=\Gamma(T,\mathcal J_i|_T)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] its associated sheaf is $\mathcal J_i|_T$, and [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine] makes $J$ finitely generated. The inverse image of $D(a)$ is $D(a_B)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-basic-open-pullback], where $a_B$ is the image of $a$ in $B$. Since $\mathcal J_i$ is the unit ideal there, [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-zero-set-affine] gives $V(J)\subset V(aB)$. Thus all hypotheses of [lem-trf-etale-ideal-local-factor] hold for $A\to B,a,J$; in particular the regular element is in $A$, as required.

source.place: Tag 0814, lemma-flatten-module-etale-localize, proof paragraph 2 (finite open refinement); Tag 0813, lemma-push-ideal.

proof.text: For every $q\in T$, [lem-trf-etale-ideal-local-factor] supplies $g_q\notin q$, a finitely generated $I_q\subset A$ with $V(I_q)\subset V(a)$, and a finitely generated $J'_q\subset B_{g_q}$ such that $I_qB_{g_q}=(JB_{g_q})J'_q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], $W_q=D_T(g_q)$ is the affine open $\operatorname{Spec}B_{g_q}$. On it let $\mathcal J'_q=\widetilde{J'_q}$; this is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] and finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine]. The sections of $\mathcal J_i$ on $W_q$ are $JB_{g_q}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-affine-section-base-change]. The extended ideal $I_q\mathcal O_{W_q}$ is generated by the images of a finite set of generators of $I_q$; on each principal open its sections are the corresponding localized ideal. By [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] the product $(\mathcal J_i|_{W_q})\mathcal J'_q$ is quasi-coherent with sections $(JB_{g_q})J'_q$. The canonical affine reconstruction in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] therefore turns the displayed ideal equality into the required equality of ideal subsheaves $I_q\mathcal O_{W_q}=(\mathcal J_i|_{W_q})\mathcal J'_q$.

source.place: Tag 0814, lemma-flatten-module-etale-localize, proof paragraph 2 (finite open refinement); Tag 0813, lemma-push-ideal.

proof.text: The opens $W_q$, one containing each $q\in T$, cover $T$. Since $T$ is quasi-compact, choose a finite subcover. Do this for each of the finitely many $T_{it}$ and each $i$ in the finite set $I$. Their finite disjoint index set is $R$, and the projection to $i$ defines $i:R\to I$. Retain the corresponding $I_q$ and $\mathcal J'_q$ as $I_r$ and $\mathcal J'_r$. In either case $S_i=\bigcup_{i(r)=i}W_r$. Empty $S_i$ contribute no opens. This uses just the definition of quasi-compactness and finite unions of finite sets.

source.place: Tag 0814, lemma-flatten-module-etale-localize, proof paragraph 2 (finite open refinement); Tag 0813, lemma-push-ideal.

proof.text: Each $W_r$ is qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Apply [lemma-nagata-open-immersion-qc-over-separated-target] to $W_r\to S\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$: the first composite is quasi-compact because $W_r$ is quasi-compact, and $S\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-separated by hypothesis. Thus $W_r\to S$ is quasi-compact, without assuming $S_i$ quasi-separated. It is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. The inverse-image open $g_i^{-1}W_r\subset X_i$, with its restricted structure map to $W_r$, represents $X_i\times_{S_i}W_r$: a map into $X_i$ whose composite lands in $W_r$ factors uniquely through this open. Hence $Y_r$ is that open subscheme, and $Y_r\to X$ is etale by the same composition lemma. For every point $s\in S$ choose $s_i\in S_i$ over it and a $W_r$ containing $s_i$. For every $x\in X$ choose $x_i\in X_i$ over it and a $W_r$ containing $g_i(x_i)$; then $x_i\in Y_r$. These choices prove both joint-surjectivity assertions. Finally $U_r=W_r\times_SU$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-morphism-preimage-qc-open].

source.place: Tag 0814, lemma-flatten-module-etale-localize, proof paragraph 2 (finite open refinement); Tag 0813, lemma-push-ideal.

proof.text: Fix $r$ and put $i=i(r)$. The module $j_i^*\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent]. In [lem-trf-module-strict-transform-flat-pullback] take $(X,S)=(X_i,S_i)$, $(Y,T)=(Y_r,W_r)$, $\mathcal I=\mathcal J_i$, and module $j_i^*\mathcal F$. Both maps $W_r\to S_i$ and $Y_r\to X_i$ are open inclusions and therefore flat: their local-ring maps are isomorphisms, so they satisfy [def-weil-flat-morphism]. The lemma identifies $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J_r}W_r$ with the inverse-image open of $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J_i}S_i$, and identifies the strict transform on $Y_r$ with the pullback, hence restriction, of the given transform. By the composition isomorphism in [def-pc-module-pullback], the module being transformed is precisely the pullback of $\mathcal F$ along $Y_r\to X$. At every point of this open restriction both the module stalk and the base local ring equal the original ones. The flat transform remains flat by the stalk criterion in [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over].

source.place: Tag 0814, lemma-flatten-module-etale-localize, proof paragraph 2 (finite open refinement); Tag 0813, lemma-push-ideal.

proof.text: Restriction preserves quasi-coherence and finite type directly from their local definitions [pqf-def-coherent]. Thus $\mathcal J_r$ is a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal and it equals the unit ideal on $U_r$. The blowup identification of step 6, together with the quasi-compactness of $U_r$ from step 5, is exactly the $U_r$-admissible blowup datum in [def-nagata-admissible-blowup]. In the affine-base case the $I_r,\mathcal J'_r$ from steps 3--4 give $V(I_r)\subset V(a)$ and $I_r\mathcal O_{W_r}=\mathcal J_r\mathcal J'_r$. This proves every required assertion.

tool_uses.why: Quasi-compact source and quasi-separated target imply the map is quasi-compact; the unit has no replacement for this scheme-theoretic permanence tool.
Converts finite type of the local ideal sheaf to finite generation of its affine section ideal, and back for the companion ideal; this generic affine module criterion is not supplied by the unit.
Identifies the vanishing locus of the restricted ideal sheaf with the affine ideal vanishing locus needed by 0813; it is a generic affine ideal tool.
Computes the restricted ideal on a principal affine open as the localized ideal; this affine quasi-coherent restriction tool is not an alternative proof route.
Computes the product ideal sheaf on the affine refinement from the product of section ideals, to transfer the 0813 factorization to sheaves.

Step 6: the module strict-transform flat-pullback lemma applies to the open immersions W_r→S_i and Y_r→X_i, which are flat; stalks are unchanged, so flatness follows from the stalk criterion.
